name: Larsen & Toubro Ltd
title: Larsen & Toubro Ltd - 500510 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Record FY26 order inflow of ₹4.36 lakh crore (+22%) and order book ₹7.40 lakh crore (+28%), but margins slipped on execution cost pressures and Q1 FY27 guidance is not in this annual-report extract.

triggers.label: Order book ₹7.40 lakh cr, +28%
triggers.quote: Your Company's Order Book stood at a record high of ₹ 7.40 lakh crore, registering a growth of 28% year-on-year.

triggers.label: MCO cost ratio 67.5% vs 66.9%
triggers.quote: mainly due to cost pressures in some projects within the portfolio of Project & Manufacturing businesses.

triggers.label: Energy margin 8.5% → 6.8%
triggers.quote: The segment's operating margin declined to 6.8% from 8.5%, mainly due to cost pressures in few legacy jobs in the Hydrocarbon business.

guidance.value: Continue EPC momentum with improved profitability; 2X workforce productivity

red_flags.label: Execution cost pressure and provisioning
red_flags.quote: Overall margin performance was impacted by execution-related time and cost pressures in the Infrastructure and Energy segments, including higher provisioning on contract assets and customer receivables.

red_flags.label: Water segment revenue decline on funding delays
red_flags.quote: The lower growth was mainly on account of Water & Effluent Treatment business which was impacted by customer project funding constraints leading to procurement delays

summary.headline: L&T FY26 Group order inflow hit a record ₹4.36 lakh crore (+22%), order book ₹7.40 lakh crore (+28%); recurring PAT ₹17,238 crore (+18%).
summary.overview: This is the FY2025-26 annual report transcript (filed as Q1 FY27 document), not a quarterly call, so figures are full-year. Group revenue rose 11.8% to ₹2,85,874 crore and PBDIT grew 10.3% to ₹29,151 crore, with EBITDA margin at 10.2%. Margins were hit by execution-related cost and time pressures in Infrastructure and Energy, including higher provisioning on contract assets and receivables. Net debt-to-equity improved to 0.35:1 from 0.60:1, and the Board recommended a final dividend of ₹38 per share. Management flagged West Asia uncertainty but said business continuity at GCC sites was intact.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Order inflow ₹1,99,064 crore (+14.9%, 46% of group inflow); revenue ₹1,35,345 crore (+3.1%); operating margin improved to 6.9% from 6.4%. Water & Effluent Treatment revenue hit by funding constraints and Jal Jeevan Mission delays.

segments.name: Energy Projects
segments.commentary: Order inflow ₹1,36,921 crore (+56.4%, driven by ultra-mega Hydrocarbon orders); revenue ₹54,889 crore (+34.9%); operating margin fell to 6.8% from 8.5% on legacy Hydrocarbon job cost pressures; 74% of revenue international.

segments.name: Hi-Tech Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Order inflow ₹8,366 crore (-54.2% on high base); revenue ₹14,489 crore (+42.3%); operating margin 16.7% vs 17.3%.

segments.name: IT & Technology Services (LTM, LTTS, others)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹53,497 crore (+11.3%), 91% international; operating margin steady at 19.5%. New platforms (data centre, semiconductor) not yet material to revenue.

segments.name: Financial Services (L&T Finance)
segments.commentary: Retail book above ₹1,19,500 crore, 98% retailised; rated AAA (domestic). Gold loan business of Paul Merchants acquired with 130 branches.

guidance_outlook: Management expects sustained demand across infrastructure, hydrocarbon, renewables, T&D, power, and water in India and abroad; SHANTI Act expected to spur small modular reactor interest.
West Asia conflict creates near-term uncertainty; clients interacted indicate project award timelines broadly aligned with original plans.
Lakshya 2031 (FY27-FY31) plan targets 2x workforce productivity, improved profitability and divestment of non-core assets.
Nabha Power divestment to Torrent Power (EV ₹6,889 crore) expected to complete in Q1 FY27; Hyderabad Metro stake sale (₹1,461.47 crore) likely by June 30, 2026.
LTM and LTTS expect challenging economic and industry conditions in FY27.
Larsen & Toubro Vyoma plans 36 MW AI-ready data centre at Mahape scalable to 100 MW over three years, subject to approvals and power availability.

qa_highlights.question: No analyst Q&A is present in the transcript; this is the FY26 annual report, not an earnings call.
qa_highlights.answer: Not applicable. Outlook statements are from the Chairman's letter and MD&A only.

qa_highlights.question: How is management handling the West Asia conflict's impact on ongoing projects?
qa_highlights.answer: The Chairman says the GCC business (about one-third of ~USD 32 billion revenue, across ~100 project sites) is business as usual with no material disruption to invoicing or collections. Management also says client interactions indicate award timelines are broadly aligned with original plans.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin pressure in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution-related time and cost pressures in Infrastructure and Energy, including higher provisioning on contract assets and customer receivables. Some savings from cost optimisation partly offset this. MCO expenses rose to 67.5% of revenue from 66.9%.

capex_capacity: Standalone capex (net) was ₹1,915 crore in FY26 vs ₹2,039 crore in FY25; group capex (net) rose to ₹4,469 crore from ₹3,541 crore.

Larsen & Toubro Vyoma operational data-centre capacity reached 26 MW across Chennai and Panvel; 24 MW of the planned 30 MW Chennai facility is commissioned, with the remaining 6 MW at an advanced stage.
Larsen & Toubro Vyoma is developing a 36 MW AI-ready green data centre at Mahape, Navi Mumbai, scalable to 100 MW over three years, subject to statutory approvals and power availability.

Hydrocarbon Offshore fabrication capacity is about 2,00,000 MT per year across Hazira, Kattupalli and Sohar; Kattupalli is being upgraded into a 'Wind Hub'. Tower fabrication capacity in T&D is over 1.1 lakh tonnes per annum.

Energy Projects execution milestones included the Jafurah Gas Compression Phase-1 and Export Pipeline commissioning, and the 3.55 MMTPA RUF at HPCL Visakhapatnam commissioned. Nuclear/CarbonLite COD for units at SJVN Buxar and Khurja was also achieved.
demand_pricing: Group order inflow ₹4,35,590 crore (+22.1%, record; international 58% of inflow). The annual report's highlights text cites ₹4.36 lakh crore; order book ₹7,40,327 crore (+27.8%), with international share at 52%.
Order book composition at 31 March 2026: government and PSU clients about 61%, private sector 39% (up from 28%). About 19% of domestic order book is multilateral-funded.

Infrastructure order inflow ₹1,99,064 crore (+14.9%), with West Asia 79% of international inflow for the segment. Energy Projects inflow ₹1,36,921 crore (+56.4%), with ultra-mega Hydrocarbon orders such as QatarEnergy NGL-5 and Saudi Aramco Zuluf.
Hi-Tech Manufacturing inflow ₹8,366 crore (-54.2%) on high base; revenue ₹14,489 crore (+42.3%). IT & TS revenue ₹53,497 crore (+11.3%), 91% international, operating margin 19.5%.

Water: JJM funding paused for review in FY26, hurting Water & Effluent Treatment revenue; government extended JJM to 2028 with ~₹67,000 crore allocation in FY27. Energy segment operating margin fell to 6.8% from 8.5% on legacy Hydrocarbon jobs.
risks_watch: Energy segment margin fell to 6.8% from 8.5% on legacy Hydrocarbon job cost pressures; watch whether these legacy jobs recover in FY27.
West Asia exposure: GCC is about one-third of revenue and 58% of order inflow is international; the annual report flags possible near-term project award and vendor payment challenges.

Gratuity one-time charge under New Labour Codes: standalone PAT fell to ₹6,287 crore after a ₹6,843 crore exceptional charge, with the LTMRHL impairment included. Confirm there are no further exceptional items.
Divestments pending: Nabha Power to Torrent Power (EV ₹6,889 crore, expected Q1 FY27 completion) and Hyderabad Metro stake sale (₹1,461.47 crore, by June 30, 2026). Check whether they closed.
LTM and LTTS guide to challenging economic and industry conditions in FY27; new platforms (data centre, semiconductor) are not yet material to revenue. Water revenue depends on JJM fund release.
key_quotes: The conflict in the region has barely impacted us. It is business as usual at the 100 odd project sites there, with no material disruption to invoicing or collections.

Overall margin performance was impacted by execution-related time and cost pressures in the Infrastructure and Energy segments, including higher provisioning on contract assets and customer receivables.
The evolving situation in West Asia creates some near-term uncertainty.
Economic and industry conditions in FY 2026-27 are expected to remain challenging.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term order visibility and balance-sheet strength, but cautious on near-term West Asia uncertainty and on FY27 conditions in LTM and LTTS. Management acknowledges execution-related margin pressure in Infrastructure and Energy without quantifying a recovery timeline.

growth.why: No explicit numeric revenue guidance for FY27; management cites sustained demand and a record ₹7.40 lakh crore order book (+28%), with 61% government/PSU clients, while the 36 MW Vyoma data centre is subject to approvals and power availability and margins were pressured by legacy Hydrocarbon jobs.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Group EBITDA margin fell to 10.2% with Energy segment margin down to 6.8% from 8.5% on legacy Hydrocarbon job cost pressures, and management gave no recovery timeline; Infrastructure margin did improve to 6.9% from 6.4%, and Nabha/Metro divestments may help reported earnings.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q1 FY27 for 6 MW; FY27-FY29 for Vyoma 36 MW
rows.why: Remaining 6 MW of the 30 MW Chennai data centre is at an advanced stage, and the 36 MW Mahape facility (scalable to 100 MW over three years) is subject to approvals and power availability; no hydrocarbon or fabrication capacity addition was announced.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Record group order book of ₹7,40,327 crore (+27.8%) and order inflow of ₹4,35,590 crore (+22.1%) back FY26 revenue growth of 11.8%, though Hi-Tech inflow fell 54.2% and LTM/LTTS expect challenging FY27 conditions.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Group net capex rose to ₹4,469 crore from ₹3,541 crore and the Vyoma data-centre build-out is planned, but utilisation was not disclosed and standalone capex fell to ₹1,915 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric revenue or margin guidance was given, and management cited margin pressure in Infrastructure and Energy and uncertainty from West Asia.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Energy margin fell to 6.8% from 8.5% on legacy Hydrocarbon jobs, provisioning rose on contract assets and receivables, and West Asia could delay award timelines, although management said GCC business is business as usual.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Larsen & Toubro Vyoma AI-ready data centre (36 MW at Mahape) and the Kattupalli Wind Hub upgrade are planned, but no launch date is firm and the brief says new platforms are not yet material to revenue.

rows.label: Record order book of ₹7.40 lakh crore
rows.why: Order book rose 27.8% to ₹7,40,327 crore with 61% government/PSU clients, providing multi-year revenue visibility, though 52% is international and West Asia exposure is high.

rows.label: Net debt-to-equity down to 0.35:1 from 0.60:1
rows.why: Net debt-to-equity fell from 0.60:1 to 0.35:1, and pending divestments (Nabha Power EV ₹6,889 crore, Hyderabad Metro stake ₹1,461.47 crore) could lower debt further.

rows.label: Legacy Hydrocarbon job margin recovery
rows.why: Energy margin fell to 6.8% from 8.5% and management gave no recovery timeline, so a rebound depends on legacy jobs being executed without further provisioning.

tone.note: Management was confident on the record order book (₹7.40 lakh crore, +28%) and balance-sheet deleveraging, but cautious on West Asia uncertainty, Energy margin pressure from legacy Hydrocarbon jobs, and challenging FY27 conditions at LTM and LTTS.
